name: Set the school's off-days and holidays, and tell families about them
priorityReason: Attendance and payroll both read it. Without it a closed day reads as everybody absent.

goal.capability: to mark which days the school is closed and broadcast notice of them
goal.outcome: attendance and payroll treat a closed day correctly, and families are told before they turn up

secondaryActors.involvement: Is governed by the calendar and sees it in their own view.
Relies on it for correct payroll and cannot change it.

additional.description: The month approaches and the calendar for it has not been set (BR-11).
An unplanned closure is declared, which is added the same day.

preconditions.condition: An academic session is open, since the calendar is set within one.
An authenticated session exists and the acting user is School Admin.
For a broadcast, a messaging channel is configured with balance.

postConditions: The month's weekly off-days and public holidays are set and applied.
Attendance marking is refused on those days, so a closed day is never recorded as an absence.
Payroll excludes them, so nobody loses a day's pay because the school was shut.
Where a broadcast was sent, every parent has been told and the send is logged with its delivery status.
A day added or removed after the fact carries a reason, and any attendance already marked on a newly closed day is flagged rather than silently discarded.
The calendar is visible to staff and to families in their own views, so nobody has to ask whether the school is open.
Accounts can read the calendar and could not have changed it.

businessRules.rule: The calendar decides which days are working days. Attendance and payroll both read it, and neither has its own idea of when the school was open.
Weekly off-days are set as a pattern and applied across the month, rather than marked one date at a time.
No attendance is marked on a closed day. A day the school was shut is not a day anybody was absent.
A holiday or a closure carries a reason. A weekly off does not, since the pattern is the explanation.
Payroll excludes closed days. Nobody loses a day's pay because the school was shut.
A day may close the whole school or only part of it. A staff training day is not a holiday for staff, and an examination day may close classes without closing the school.
Accounts read the calendar and cannot change it. The role that calculates pay must not be the role that decides which days are paid.
A broadcast is sent through the messaging channels and every send is logged with its delivery status. Nothing is reported as delivered that the provider did not confirm.
A day already set may be removed, with a reason. Governments move holidays, and the calendar has to be able to follow.
Where a day is closed after attendance was already marked on it, the existing marks are flagged rather than silently discarded. Somebody decides what to do with them.
A month whose calendar has not been set is flagged before it begins, because an unset month means attendance opens on days the school is shut.
An unplanned closure may be added on the day itself. A school closed for weather does not wait for a calendar cycle.

transitions.condition: Removed with a reason after notice was sent, which normally needs a further broadcast.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Attendance → Off-day calendar → Month view
basicFlow.userAction: Opens the calendar for the coming month.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Shows the month with any days already set.

basicFlow.userAction: Marks the days of the week the school is normally closed.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Applies the pattern across the month rather than requiring each date to be marked.

basicFlow.userAction: Adds each public or school holiday with its reason and what it closes.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Requires a reason for anything other than a weekly off, and records what the day closes.

basicFlow.userAction: Saves the calendar for the month.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Applies it, so attendance marking is refused on those days and payroll excludes them.

basicFlow.userAction: Sends notice to parents, telling them the school is closed.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Sends through the messaging channels and logs each send with its delivery status.
Makes the calendar visible to staff and to families in their own views.

basicFlow.userAction: Removes a day where the holiday has moved, giving a reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Removes it with the reason recorded, and flags any attendance already marked around the change.

alternateFlows.condition: The day closes only part of the school
alternateFlows.navigation: Month view → Add holiday → Applies to
alternateFlows.behaviour: The day is scoped to students only, staff only or selected classes. A staff training day is not a holiday for staff (BR-6).

alternateFlows.condition: The school closes unexpectedly for weather
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Attendance → Off-day calendar → Add holiday
alternateFlows.behaviour: The closure is added on the day itself and broadcast at once. A school closed for weather does not wait for a calendar cycle (BR-12).

alternateFlows.condition: A government notification moves a public holiday
alternateFlows.navigation: Off-day calendar → Remove a day, then Add holiday
alternateFlows.behaviour: The original is removed with its reason and the new date added. Both changes are recorded and a further broadcast normally follows (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: Attendance was already marked on a day now closed
alternateFlows.navigation: Off-day calendar → Remove a day → Affected attendance
alternateFlows.behaviour: The existing marks are flagged for a decision rather than silently discarded, since somebody recorded them for a reason (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: The School Admin wants to announce something other than a holiday
alternateFlows.behaviour: The broadcast carries any notice the school needs to send, not only a closure. It is the same route and the same log.

alternateFlows.condition: The month has not been set as it approaches
alternateFlows.behaviour: The unset month is flagged before it begins, because an unset month means attendance opens on days the school is shut (BR-11).

departures.requirement: Attendance, payroll and the timetable all read this one calendar. No module holds its own idea of when the school was open.
An unplanned closure takes effect immediately on saving, without waiting for an overnight job, because a school closed for weather needs it now.
A broadcast reads Queued until the provider confirms otherwise, and failures are listed per recipient.

openQuestions.question: Which days are the school's normal weekly off-days?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and the pattern differs between schools.

openQuestions.question: When attendance already exists on a day that is later closed, what should happen to those marks?
openQuestions.assumption: They are flagged, but who decides and what they decide is not specified.

openQuestions.question: Should the calendar be set per branch, or once for the whole school?
openQuestions.assumption: Per branch as modelled. Not confirmed, and public holidays are the same everywhere.

openQuestions.question: Is the broadcast sent automatically when a closure is added, or only on request?
openQuestions.assumption: On request. Confirm the school does not want it automatic for unplanned closures.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: bulk-actions
conventionsApplied.rule: Any bulk operation reports a per-row result, commits valid rows and lists rejected rows with the reason. A bulk action never fails as a whole because of one bad row.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
